description: Taurus zodiac sign: personality traits, strengths and challenges, love, career, decans and dates (April 20 to May 20).
answer: In Western astrology, Taurus is the second sign of the zodiac, a fixed earth sign ruled by Venus. It is traditionally associated with steadiness, sensual pleasure, patience and quiet determination. The Sun is in Taurus from about April 20 to May 20. The exact dates shift by a day from year to year.

sections.heading: Taurus personality traits
paragraphs: Taurus is the zodiac's great consolidator. Where the sign before it strikes the match, Taurus builds the hearth and keeps it burning. Its symbol, the Bull, captures the paradox neatly: calm, content to graze and slow to stir, yet immovable once it decides to stand its ground. People with strong Taurus placements tend to trust what they can touch, taste and test over time, and they are often wary of anything that arrives with too much hurry or hype. There is a deep appreciation for comfort and craft here, for good bread, well-made shoes, music that rewards repeated listening and friendships that have weathered decades.

Astrologically, Taurus is a fixed earth sign ruled by Venus. Earth signs concern themselves with the physical and the practical: bodies, money, materials, the things that sustain a life. Fixed signs hold and deepen rather than begin, which gives the Bull its famous persistence. Venus, often linked only with romance, also governs beauty, value and pleasure, and in this sign that influence turns earthy and sensual. The combination describes a person who usually knows what they like, builds security slowly and enjoys life through the senses. Where other signs chase ideas, Taurus asks a simpler question: does this actually feel good, and will it last?

sections.heading: Taurus strengths and challenges
paragraphs: Reliability is the quality people most often prize in a Taurus. When this sign commits to a job, a friend or a plan, it tends to stay the course long after the novelty has faded for everyone else. It is usually unhurried and hard to rattle, which makes it a soothing presence in a crisis. Many Bulls have a practical genius for making a home comfortable and beautiful on a modest budget, along with a good instinct for what is worth paying for. Add loyalty, a dry sense of humour and unshowy competence with physical tasks, from cooking to gardening to building, and Taurus becomes the friend everyone calls when something needs doing properly.

The same steadiness can harden into stubbornness. Taurus may dig in simply because it has been pushed, defending a position long after its reasons have faded. Change, especially sudden change imposed by others, can feel threatening, and the Bull sometimes stays in situations that no longer serve it because leaving would mean upheaval. Possessiveness can creep in, over people as well as things. There is also a tendency to let comfort slide into inertia, postponing the difficult conversation or the overdue move in favour of another quiet evening in. And because it is slow to anger, resentment can build unseen until it finally erupts, surprising everyone, sometimes even Taurus itself.

sections.heading: Taurus in love and relationships
paragraphs: Taurus tends to fall in love slowly and stay for a long time. Early on it may seem reserved, watching whether a potential partner is consistent before opening up. Once committed, though, it offers a rare kind of devotion: physical affection, thoughtful gifts, meals made with care and a steady presence that makes a partner feel safe. The Bull expresses love through the senses and through dependability far more than through grand speeches. It needs loyalty, a calm home life and plenty of touch. Inconsistency unsettles it deeply, and someone who keeps changing plans or moods may find Taurus quietly withdrawing to protect itself.

Conflict with a Taurus usually centres on flexibility. A partner who craves spontaneity or frequent change may meet resistance, while the Bull can feel pressured or destabilised. Jealousy is the other common sore point. Giving it time works wonders: proposals made gently and revisited a few days later tend to land far better than demands made on the spot. Shared rituals, such as a weekly dinner or an evening walk, strengthen the bond because they build the predictability Taurus finds romantic. Virgo and Capricorn are traditionally considered natural allies, and Cancer and Pisces often treasure the emotional security this sign provides so readily.

sections.heading: Taurus at work
paragraphs: Professionally, Taurus is the steady engine rather than the flashy spark. It tends to excel where patience, consistency and attention to quality matter: banking, property, agriculture, architecture, design, cooking, music and any craft that improves with years of practice. The Bull usually prefers clear structure and tangible results over constant reinvention, and it often builds expertise quietly until it becomes the person everyone relies on. As a manager it is typically calm and fair, slow to make changes but dependable once a direction is set. Colleagues tend to trust a Taurus boss because a promise made is, in their experience, generally a promise kept.

The pitfalls appear when a workplace demands rapid change. Taurus can resist new systems, cling to methods that once worked and miss openings that require a leap. It may also linger in a secure but unfulfilling job for years. Money is often an area of natural skill: this sign tends to save well, buy quality and think about long-term value, though it can overspend on comfort and beautiful objects. Its relationship with security deserves an honest look, since the wish for safety can keep the Bull from the very risks that would serve its ambitions. Reviewing goals once or twice a year helps it move with intention rather than habit.

sections.heading: Growth and the three Taurus decans
paragraphs: For Taurus, growth often means making friends with change. A good starting point is small, voluntary disruptions: a different route to work, an unfamiliar cuisine, a class in something it has never tried. These build tolerance for novelty in a setting the Bull controls, which makes bigger transitions less frightening when they come. It also helps to notice the difference between principled persistence and plain stubbornness by asking, in the middle of a disagreement, what would genuinely change its mind. Voicing irritation early, in small doses, prevents the long build-up behind the rare explosive moments. Finally, Taurus thrives when it treats pleasure as nourishment rather than escape, choosing comforts that restore energy over those that simply numb.

Taurus divides into three decans of ten degrees each. The first, roughly April 20 to April 29, belongs to Venus; the second, about April 30 to May 10, to Mercury; and the third, around May 11 to May 20, to Saturn. Each has its own page, and every Taurus birthday links to its decan.

faq.question: Why are Taurus people so stubborn?
faq.answer: Taurus is a fixed sign, and fixed signs are traditionally linked with holding steady. That firmness protects what the Bull has built, but it can turn into resistance when change is needed. Giving a Taurus time and clear reasons usually works far better than pressure.

faq.question: What does a Taurus need in a relationship?
faq.answer: Consistency, physical affection and loyalty top the list. Taurus tends to feel loved through steady presence, shared comforts and promises kept, and is often unsettled by unpredictability or emotional games. Patience in the early stages is usually rewarded with deep, lasting devotion.

faq.question: What are the dates for Taurus?
faq.answer: About April 20 to May 20. The Sun's entry into each sign moves by a day or so between years, so birthdays at either end are cusp dates; the zodiac sign calculator settles them for a specific year.

faq.question: What are the three Taurus decans?
faq.answer: The first decan (0° to 9°) is linked with Venus, the second (10° to 19°) with Mercury and the third (20° to 29°) with Saturn, following the rulers of the earth signs in zodiac order.
